title: Distordia Agreement Standard (v0.2.0 draft)
description: Generic two-party commitment primitive: request -> COUNTERPARTY-SIGNED offer -> terms-locked agreement -> NATIVE settlement. Successor to the MissionContract half of swarm.v0.1.0, and the shared replacement for nexgo-ride's bespoke offer/agreement types. Custody is NOT modelled here: funds are held by a native Nexus CONDITIONAL CONTRACT (or Invoice), which releases on conditions and is redeemable by the sender after expiry. This removes v0.1.0's custodial, Distordia-mediated escrow (a mutable integer plus a 2% fee and a 50 DIST dispute fee). See docs/agent-swarm-nexus-alignment-note.md.
supersedesStandard: the MissionContract definition of swarm.v0.1.0.json (retained for history); also supersedes nexgo-ride-offer and nexgo-ride-agreement from nexgo-ride.v0.2.0
maxSize: 1KB per asset (system fields ~180 bytes, ~820 bytes for data). Detailed terms/specifications live off-chain via spec-uri and are integrity-checked by spec-hash.

principles.mutualConsent: Each party writes on its OWN sigchain: the requester creates the request, the offeror creates the offer, the requester creates the agreement referencing that offer. No party can assert another party's consent -- the defect this fixes in both swarm.v0.1.0 (one asset, one signer) and nexgo-ride.v0.1.0 (passenger asserted the driver's acceptance).
principles.nativeCustody: The agreement REFERENCES a native conditional contract / invoice that actually holds value. Nexus conditional contracts release funds when conditions evaluate true and become redeemable by the sender after a set period -- giving deadline-plus-refund semantics natively. Never store escrow as a mutable integer.
principles.noOperatorInTheMiddle: There is no protocol fee to Distordia and no Distordia-held escrow. Disputes route to arbitration agreed by the parties; Nexus explicitly supports non-custodial escrow and arbitration.
principles.derivedReputation: Track record is computed by querying agreements where a namespace is party-a or party-b, filtered by final status. Never stored as self-written counters.
principles.domainProfiles: A domain MAY define its own request type when domain-specific fields must be queryable for discovery (e.g. nexgo-ride-request needs pickup/dest geohash). Domains MUST use the generic offer and agreement types below, because that is where the shape is genuinely identical.

assetTypes.description: Generic open request for goods, services or work. Created on the requester's sigchain.

self-addr.description: Queryable copy of this asset's register address; referenced by offers as 'request'.

domain.description: Application domain, so one primitive serves many use cases and consumers can filter.

requester.description: Requesting NAMESPACE. Nexus namespace rules apply: lowercase letters, numbers and periods only (hyphens are INVALID on-chain).

summary.description: Short human-readable statement of what is wanted. Full terms belong in the off-chain spec.

spec-uri.description: Location of the detailed specification (ar:// / ipfs:// / https).

spec-hash.description: SHA-256 of the specification, so both parties provably agreed to the same terms.

qty.description: Quantity requested (integer; use the smallest unit to avoid floats).

unit.description: Unit of the quantity (e.g. EA, KG, HR, KM).

max-price-milli.description: Maximum acceptable price in milli-units of 'currency' (integer; divide by 1000).

deliver-by-ts.description: Unix time by which delivery/performance is required.

expires-ts.description: Unix expiry after which offerors should ignore this request.

assetTypes.description: COUNTERPARTY-SIGNED offer against a request, created on the OFFEROR'S OWN sigchain. This is the on-chain consent handshake; an agreement is only valid if it references a real offer authored by the counterparty.

self-addr.description: Queryable copy of this asset's register address; referenced by the agreement as 'offer'.

request.description: self-addr of the distordia-request (or domain request profile) being bid on.

offeror.description: Offering NAMESPACE -- the owner of this asset, which is what makes the offer self-signed. Nexus namespace rules apply: lowercase letters, numbers and periods only (hyphens are INVALID on-chain).

price-milli.description: Offered price in milli-units of 'currency'. MUST be <= the request's max-price-milli.

deliver-by-ts.description: Unix time the offeror commits to deliver by.

eta-sec.description: Optional estimated seconds until start/arrival (used by time-sensitive domains such as nexgo.ride).

resource.description: Optional self-addr of the asset backing this offer -- e.g. a nexgo-taxi vehicle, an agent-card, or a product record.

assetTypes.description: The requester accepts one specific offer. Price and terms are LOCKED, both parties are recorded, and settlement is delegated to a native conditional contract / invoice.

self-addr.description: Queryable copy of this asset's register address; referenced by ratings, deliverables and reputation queries.

domain.description: Application domain, copied from the request.

offer.description: self-addr of the ACCEPTED counterparty-signed offer. This reference is the proof of mutual consent.

party-a.description: Requesting NAMESPACE (buyer). Nexus namespace rules apply: lowercase letters, numbers and periods only (hyphens are INVALID on-chain).

party-b.description: Performing NAMESPACE (seller). Nexus namespace rules apply: lowercase letters, numbers and periods only (hyphens are INVALID on-chain).

price-milli.description: LOCKED price in milli-units of 'currency', equal to the accepted offer's price. The native contract/invoice amount MUST equal this.

contract.description: Reference to the NATIVE Nexus conditional contract or invoice that actually holds and releases value. Custody lives there, not in this record -- there is deliberately no 'escrow' integer field.

deliver-by-ts.description: Unix delivery deadline. Enforcement is native: if conditions are not satisfied, the conditional contract becomes redeemable by the sender after its expiry period.

proof-hash.description: SHA-256 of off-chain delivery evidence (delivery note, trip record, inspection report). The chain anchors the evidence; judging real-world performance remains an oracle/arbitration function.

droppedFromSwarmV010.escrow: Custodial integer replaced by a reference to a native conditional contract that actually holds funds.
droppedFromSwarmV010.payment-type: Redundant: settlement semantics are expressed by the native contract's conditions.
droppedFromSwarmV010.penalty-late / penalty-max: Native contract expiry/redemption provides deadline-plus-refund. Bespoke penalties may be encoded as contract conditions.
droppedFromSwarmV010.final-payment: Derived from the settled contract, not asserted.
droppedFromSwarmV010.dispute-reason + 50 DIST filing fee + 2%: Removed with the operator-in-the-middle model; disputes route to arbitration agreed by the parties.
droppedFromSwarmV010.contractor-swarm / contractee-swarm: A swarm is just a party (an agent-card with kind='swarm'); no separate field needed.
droppedFromSwarmV010.progress: A mutable self-reported percentage proves nothing; status transitions plus proof-hash are verifiable.

examples._comment: A swarm mission expressed as a generic request.
examples.summary: Deliver 1000 widget units from Factory A to Warehouse B

examples._comment: The agreement: both parties consented, price locked, custody delegated to a native contract.

nexus.settlement: Fund and settle via native conditional contracts (or the Invoices API for simple pay-on-delivery, as nexgo.ride does). The contract amount MUST equal the agreement's price-milli.

notes: One primitive replaces swarm-mission and nexgo-ride's bespoke offer/agreement types; product.sourcing can reuse it for purchase commitments.
Mutual consent is structural: each party writes on its own sigchain, and the agreement's 'offer' reference proves the counterparty actually agreed.
Custody is native. There is intentionally NO escrow integer, no protocol fee, and no operator holding funds.
Reputation and track record are derived by querying settled/failed agreements per namespace -- see the ecosystem-wide finding that reputation must have provenance.
Domains may define request profiles with queryable domain fields (e.g. nexgo-ride-request), but MUST use the generic offer and agreement.
